title: CI plan: eval gates + quality guardrails (Optimize)
content:
Context
- Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quant profile) are now gated by offline evals + thresholds before apply/promotion.
- CI must prevent regressions in the gating system itself (state machine, contracts, enforcement, audit events) without turning every PR into a multi-hour GPU burn.
- Constraint: GPU capacity is scarce/variable; we need predictable required checks and clear fallbacks.

Non-goals (for CI)
- CI does NOT run full production-grade prompt set suites on every PR.
- CI does NOT validate model quality for every change; it validates correctness, enforcement, and contract stability.

Guiding principles
1) “Enforcement correctness > quality result” in CI: prove we block/allow/override correctly; do not re-litigate threshold calibration per PR.
2) Tiered checks: cheap checks required on every PR; expensive checks on merge queue / nightly.
3) Deterministic by default: reduce flakes via fixed seeds, pinned prompt subset, pinned baselines, and clear rerun policy.
4) Defense-in-depth: at least one required check per enforcement boundary (Optimize apply endpoint + rollout promotion).
5) Explicit GPU budgeting: CI jobs must declare GPU needs and time budgets; jobs must fail fast if they cannot start in time.

What counts as “gating-related code” (impacts required checks)
- Optimize service: gate-run state machine, persistence, enforcement at apply boundary, retry/timeout handling, baseline selection (esp. quant).
- Eval-harness integration: trigger API client, response parsing, artifact linking, result aggregation.
- Config-diff schema + static validation rules.
- Rollout controller coupling: promotion blocked on gate failure.
- Console API surface for gate summaries/artifacts (required only for contract tests, not for UI rendering).
- Observability emission for gate decisions (metrics/log schema stability).

Change detection (how we decide which checks are required)
- Repo: redwood (monorepo)
- If PR touches any of these paths, “Quality Gates Required Checks” is enforced:
  - services/optimize/**
  - services/eval-client/** (if exists) / integrations/eval-harness/**
  - packages/config-diff-schema/**
  - services/rollout-controller/**
  - packages/audit-log/** (gate decision events)
  - packages/observability/** (gate metrics names/tags)
- Additionally, if PR modifies any gating policy defaults / config files:
  - config/gating-policies/**
  - config/optimize/**

CI pipeline overview (required checks)
A) Always-required (no GPU)
1) Lint + typecheck
   - Standard repo checks.
2) Unit tests (Optimize gating state machine + enforcement)
   - Validate state transitions: pending -> running -> passed/failed -> (optional) overridden.
   - Validate idempotency on retries (same gate_run_id) and cancelation behavior.
3) Schema & validation tests (config diff)
   - Golden JSON fixtures; ensure rejection reasons are stable and mapped to user-facing failure codes.
4) Contract tests (Optimize <-> eval-harness interface)
   - Uses a local stub server with recorded fixtures.
   - Verifies request payload: config diff, baseline pointer, suite selection (smoke/full), policy id, time budget.
   - Verifies response parsing: metrics, deltas, confidence/variance fields, artifacts pointers, flake_score.
5) Rollout controller enforcement tests (no GPU)
   - Ensure canary promotion API checks gate status and fails closed if gate result missing.
6) Audit event schema tests
   - Ensure gate.started, gate.completed, gate.failed, gate.overridden emit required fields.

B) Merge-queue required (GPU optional but strongly preferred; has fallback)
These run when a PR enters merge queue (or on main branch pre-merge in our queue system).
1) “E2E gating enforcement (smoke)”
   - Spins up ephemeral Optimize + eval-harness (real service) + a toy model runtime (or lightweight runner).
   - Runs a minimal smoke suite (e.g., 50-100 prompts) using pinned prompt set ids.
   - Goal: validate end-to-end flow: config diff -> eval trigger -> result aggregation -> apply allowed/blocked -> artifacts linked.
   - Target wall time: 12–18 minutes on 1x GPU.
   - Required behaviors validated:
     - Fail closed if eval-harness returns malformed/partial results.
     - Retry policy for transient errors; respects max retry budget.
     - Correct mapping of gate failure reason codes.
     - Override flow requires approver role; override expiry enforced.

C) Nightly (GPU required; non-blocking for PR merge but blocks next-day release candidate cut if red)
1) “Full suite regression (gating reliability)”
   - Runs on main against a broader prompt set (tiered suites: smoke + medium).
   - Tracks flake_score trends and job runtime distribution.
   - Primary output: gating system health (not model quality tuning).
2) “Multi-SKU quant baseline selection verification”
   - Validates baseline resolution logic across representative model families + GPU SKUs.
   - Ensures we don’t silently choose incompatible baselines.

GPU capacity strategy
- GPU job classes
  - CI-SMOKE (merge queue): 1x GPU, 20 min hard timeout, 1 retry max.
  - CI-NIGHTLY (nightly): 1–4x GPU depending on suite, 2 hour budget.
- Dedicated CI GPU pool
  - Separate from production inference capacity.
  - Hard concurrency cap (initial proposal: 6 concurrent CI-SMOKE jobs, 2 concurrent CI-NIGHTLY jobs).
- Queueing
  - Merge-queue jobs are priority; nightly yields.
  - If CI-SMOKE cannot start within 10 minutes, it triggers fallback mode (see below).

Fallback strategies (when GPU is unavailable)
We need deterministic behavior so merges don’t deadlock, while still protecting us.

Fallback mode for merge-queue “E2E gating enforcement (smoke)”
- If GPU cannot be allocated within 10 minutes OR the GPU job fails due to infra scarcity (explicit reason codes only), we switch to:
  1) CPU-only “mock runner” path (required)
     - Eval-harness executes a synthetic suite with deterministic outputs (no model inference), designed to exercise scoring, delta computation plumbing, artifact generation, and pass/fail threshold enforcement.
     - Verifies end-to-end request/response, state machine, and enforcement boundaries.
     - Note: does NOT validate runtime/model correctness; it validates gating machinery.
  2) “Stale artifact replay” (optional, only if (1) passes)
     - Replays a previously recorded eval-harness result blob to ensure Optimize accepts and enforces it.
- If fallback mode is used, the merge queue annotates the PR with: “GPU smoke skipped due to capacity; CPU fallback passed.”
- Policy: if fallback mode is used > N times in a 24h window (proposal: N=10), Release Eng will pause merge queue for gating-touched PRs until GPU pool recovers (prevents accumulating risk).

What is NOT an acceptable fallback
- Blindly skipping all E2E checks for gating-touched PRs.
- Marking GPU job as “allowed to fail” without enforcing CPU fallback.

Rerun policy and flake handling
- For CI-SMOKE (merge queue)
  - Automatic rerun: 1 rerun max, only if failure classified as “infrastructure/transient” (e.g., node preemption, networking to artifact store).
  - If flake_score from eval-harness is above threshold (e.g., >0.35) and failure is near boundary, job should re-run once with a different seed but identical prompt set.
  - If second run disagrees (pass then fail / fail then pass), mark as “FLAKY” and block merge; require manual triage label from oncall (Sahana/Connor rotation) or quarantine of suite.
- For nightly
  - Auto-rerun up to 2 times; aggregate results. Persist flake_score trend.

Timeouts and budgets
- CI-SMOKE hard timeout: 20 minutes end-to-end.
- Eval-harness sub-time budget: 12 minutes (leaves time for environment startup + artifact upload).
- Optimize waiting window for eval completion in tests: 15 minutes; must handle cancelation cleanly.

Artifact and logging requirements (CI)
- Every E2E job must upload:
  - Gate run summary JSON (state, suite, thresholds, deltas)
  - Eval-harness artifact pointers (even if synthetic)
  - Optimize enforcement decision trace (why blocked/allowed)
- Artifacts stored in the CI artifact store with retention:
  - Merge queue: 14 days
  - Nightly: 30 days
- Logs must include gate_run_id and config_diff_id for grep/triage.

Required GitHub checks (names to implement)
- quality-gates/lint-typecheck
- quality-gates/unit-optimize
- quality-gates/schema-validation
- quality-gates/contracts-eval-harness
- quality-gates/rollout-controller-enforcement
- quality-gates/audit-events-schema
- quality-gates/e2e-smoke (merge queue; GPU preferred; CPU fallback allowed under conditions)

Release cut rules (for RC builds)
- RC cut is blocked if:
  - Nightly gating reliability is red on main within the last 24 hours AND failure is not classified as infra.
  - Flake rate exceeds threshold for 2 consecutive nights (proposal: >8% flaky runs).
  - CI-SMOKE has been running in fallback mode >25% of the time over 48 hours (signals persistent GPU shortage).

Owner/rotation for CI health
- Primary: Connor O’Brien
- Backup: Sahana Iyer
- Escalation: Sean Gallagher (if GPU scarcity is impacting delivery) + Olivia Grant (if eval-harness reliability is root cause)

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide final thresholds for “GPU scarcity pause” (N per 24h) with SRE input.
- Implement explicit failure reason codes in CI runners so we can distinguish infra scarcity vs real test failure.
- Confirm whether we can reserve 1–2 A10G nodes solely for merge-queue smoke, vs shared pool.
- Align naming of gate decision audit events with Security (Marcus Lin) before checks become required.

Notes to self (Connor)
- Make sure required check list aligns with ENG-3931 and doesn’t block unrelated PRs (path filter correctness is critical).
- Keep the CPU synthetic suite maintained alongside eval-harness API versioning; otherwise it becomes a false sense of safety.
